newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police arrest two for apartment house fire.
newsitem.headline: German police arrest two for apartment house fire.

text.p: German police in the northern town of Kiel said they arrested two youths on Tuesday suspected of starting a fire in an apartment building where many foreigners live.
A police spokesman said 13 people were injured in the fire, including three who were in intensive care at a local hospital. Firefighters rescued 35 people from the fire on Monday night.
The spokesman said the two youths, aged 15 and 17, had admitted starting the fire.
"A racist motive for the crime has not been ruled out," the Kiel police spokesman said.
A third youth was released after being questioned.
Firefighters rescued 35 people from the blaze on Monday night.
Kiel, a city of 245,000 people on the Baltic Sea, is about 60 km (40 miles) north of Luebeck, where 10 people were killed in a January fire at a foreigners' hostel.
State prosecutors said that fire was started by a Lebanese man who lived in the house. He is now on trial charged with aggravated arson and causing bodily harm.
The fire in Kiel came a day after a blaze in Rickling, about 50 km (30 miles) to the south, where nine women psychiatric patients were killed.
